answer_1.quote: In this section, we define favoritism and derive a score to quantify it. Our view of favoritism is fundamentally relative, since it is based on comparing the behaviour of a metric with respect to the ground-truth provided by humans.
answer_1.outputs: The paper evaluates generated outputs from multiple NLG tasks including machine translation, summarization, and dialogue systems using both human and automated metrics.

answer_2.quote: Instead of showing the outputs of two generative systems to human raters, one uses an automatic metric and hopes that the evaluation will resemble the ratings of the humans.

answer_3.quote: Additionally to metrics participating in the WMT-22 metrics shared task, we include ratings from GPT3.5-Turbo (0613) (OpenAI, 2023) prompted as a preference metric.

answer_4.quote: There are 500 ratings by expert translators for each of the translation systems, thus, |E| = 500.
